name: AI-assisted SEO retainer via Upwork
one_liner: Win monthly SEO retainers on Upwork and use AI to do the work, starting with no prior SEO experience.
customer: Small businesses and site owners hiring SEO freelancers on Upwork
offer: Ongoing SEO work (content, on-page optimisation) delivered with AI tools
how_it_makes_money: Monthly retainer; the first client paid $3,000/month and the operator reached about $52K/month in 9 months
startup_cost: low (no amount stated beyond Upwork connects and AI subscriptions)
time_to_first_revenue: Weeks: first job came after 7 applications
evidence: 'the very first money that I made online, which is $3,000 a month retainer' (lG5U30gKCaY)
'first job she got after seven applications ... $3,000 a month for SEO and she knew nothing about SEO' (lG5U30gKCaY)
Went from zero to $52,000/month in 9 months while working 1-2 hours a day alongside a 9-5 job (lG5U30gKCaY)
risks: Outlier result; the headline income may include course or coaching revenue
Delivering without real SEO skill risks churn and refunds
Upwork competition and fees

name: Subcontracted home service brand (cleaning / holiday lighting)
one_liner: Own the customer acquisition and brand for a local home service, and subcontract all the physical work.
customer: Homeowners and businesses in a local area
offer: Cleaning or seasonal holiday-lighting installation, done by subcontractors
how_it_makes_money: Charge per job and keep the margin over what subcontractors cost; $81K revenue in month 3, with $54K already booked for the following month
time_to_first_revenue: Days to weeks; $81K/month reached within 85 days
evidence: 'in August, we did 81,000 in revenue ... 85 days' (9U4MCbfL8MQ)
'$500 of setup and we were ready to go' (9U4MCbfL8MQ)
Sold an earlier cleaning business for 'multiple six figures' (9U4MCbfL8MQ)
risks: The digest doesn't say clearly which service produced the $81K
Holiday lighting is seasonal
Quality control and liability when using subcontractors
In the UK this would be local and in-person to run

name: Leased event venue (rent-and-sublet space)
one_liner: Lease a cheap retail unit, fit it out lightly, and rent it by the event for parties, with recurring weekly tenants such as churches.
customer: Families hosting birthdays and anniversaries; churches and groups needing weekly space
how_it_makes_money: Event booking fees averaging about $16K/month (peak $22.5K); 3 churches renting every Sunday cover the lease
time_to_first_revenue: Weeks; $100 of Facebook ads produced $10K in bookings
evidence: 'Spend $100 on Facebook ads and got $10,000 in bookings' (_gI1zkOTdVU)
'Our highest month has been 22.5 ... on average we're right at like 16' (_gI1zkOTdVU)
risks: Lease liability
UK planning/use class and licensing rules
Damage and cleaning between events
Weekend work

name: Unstaffed private room rental by the hour
one_liner: Rent out a small private room (for example a karaoke booth) by the hour with self check-in by door code, and no staff.
customer: Groups and individuals wanting private space for an evening
offer: Hourly access to a private room via a code that expires when the booking ends
how_it_makes_money: $30-150/hour; one booth booked about 11 hours/week at $50/hour brings in about $1,800/month against roughly $15/hour running cost
evidence: 'A private room rents for 30 to 150 dollars an hour' (QAx2ZQNwxrA)
'One booth, booked around 11 hours a week at 50 dollars an hour, brings in roughly 1800 dollars a month' (QAx2ZQNwxrA)
'A room like that costs about 15 dollars an hour to run' (QAx2ZQNwxrA)
risks: Listicle-style source with no named operator
Lease and fit-out costs
Misuse of an unsupervised space
Local licensing

name: Kids' woodworking parties and classes
one_liner: Run woodworking birthday parties and shop classes for children aged 7-18, then add school and education-funding contracts.
customer: Parents, schools, and state-funded education programmes
offer: Woodworking birthday parties, classes and holiday camps
how_it_makes_money: $75/hour per child; spring break week brought in $12K; a $30K contract for 2 hours every Friday; $50.6K revenue from March to July
time_to_first_revenue: Days: started from a single Facebook post
evidence: 'Moms pay him 75 bucks an hour per kid' (qUORStgkuzc)
'I just signed a $30,000 contract for this fall' (qUORStgkuzc)
risks: In-person and time-bound, so a poor fit for an async-first founder
UK DBS checks, insurance and safety rules for children
The Florida state funding route has no direct UK equivalent
